Apple announced it will extend the free satellite feature usage period for existing iPhone users by another year, according to a footnote in the iPhone 18 Pro press release. Here are the details.

Apple confirms new round of extension

Apple first introduced satellite connectivity on iPhone with the iPhone 14 series, initially offering "Satellite Emergency SOS" and the ability to share location via "Find My" through satellite. Apple stated at the time that the free usage period would be two years.

Apple has since continued to expand its satellite services, adding features such as "Roadside Assistance via Satellite" and "Messages via Satellite." Apple now refers to these features collectively as satellite features.

In November 2023, Apple extended the free usage period of "Satellite Emergency SOS" for existing iPhone 14 users by another year. Last year, Apple extended the free period once again, this time covering existing users of both iPhone 14 and iPhone 15.

If not extended, the free usage period for some users would have expired later this year. However, Apple announced yesterday in a footnote of the iPhone 18 Pro press release that the free usage period will be extended for another year, and for the first time, existing iPhone 16 users will be included in the coverage.

The original press release text is as follows:

Since Apple provides one year of free satellite features for every new iPhone buyer, this means users who purchase the new iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo will enjoy one year free, while existing iPhone 14, iPhone 15, and iPhone 16 users covered by the extension programme will also receive an additional year of free usage.

Apple has yet to announce pricing after the free period ends. Given that these features could be a matter of life and death, many speculate that Apple may ultimately keep at least some of them free, as charging users for emergency services could spark controversy.

Regardless, the free usage period has been extended for another year. Whether this is the last extension, or whether we will publish a similar report next year, remains unknown.

Do you think Apple will charge for satellite features in the future? Let us know in the comments.
